security_concerns.title: Owned candidate admission does not reject descendant reparse points before native build writes
security_concerns.detail: candidate_admission/Resolve check the candidate and its immediate children only. An otherwise owned candidate with a normal VintageCardCollector_Data directory and a junction at VintageCardCollector_Data/Managed is admitted. BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer subsequently receives that existing output tree; native writes can be redirected outside the admitted candidate. The post-build recursive manifest cannot prevent an earlier write. This is a pre-existing descendant-junction case, not a race-only allegation.
security_concerns.reproduction: Fresh disposable owned fixture admitted the nested Managed junction in both actual Python candidate_admission and compiled production C# Resolve; no BuildPlayer or Unity was invoked, the target canary stayed unchanged, and junctions were removed.
security_concerns.required_fix: Before candidate mutation/native launch, recursively reject existing reparse/nonregular descendants in the candidate write tree, with the existing populated-Saves refusal preserved. Add negative tests that assert refusal before marker/output writes; apply the same protection to Python preflight and direct C# menu admission.

security_concerns.title: Owned stage admission ignores Unity-writable noncompiler directories
security_concerns.detail: stage_preflight scans Assets/Packages/ProjectSettings and selected receipt paths, but leaves an existing stage/Library junction uninspected. stage_exact retains Library; reuse-stage has the same blind spot. RequireOwnedStage/Admit likewise do not inspect Library. Launching Unity with this project path can redirect its implicit Library/cache writes outside the exact owned stage before executeMethod admission. Exact compiler-source closure does not constrain this output path.
security_concerns.reproduction: A disposable stage made by production stage_exact, with an intact owner marker and a Library junction, passed stage_preflight(restage=True). Compiled production C# RequireOwnedStage also accepted that stage. The production no_reparse helper independently rejected the same junction, establishing the omitted traversal. No Unity was launched.
security_concerns.required_fix: Preflight the complete existing Unity stage write boundary, including Library/Temp/Logs/UserSettings and other noncompiler descendants, before evidence/ownership writes, deletion, reuse or Unity launch. Reject reparse points rather than traversing their targets; do not weaken the separate preservation pruning of old-player Saves/Logs.

suggestions.detail: Strengthen native scene readback with enabled/active component and camera/listener checks, exact displayLabel/allowedProjectRoot comparisons, and explicit null optional cardBack/wrapperBack/Base-template/wrapper entries. Current creation assigns the intended values, but native validation does not cover all of them.

Validate an explicit minimum/exact toolPins key set and binding schema in the Python preflight. Present code rejects changed listed hashes but accepts any nonempty toolPins subset; parent receipt construction must currently guarantee coverage. Keep exact approved source hashes compiled in Phase5InputPolicy, not supplied arbitrarily.

Token-presence tests are useful source-contract checks but do not execute native lifecycle/resource/scene semantics. Retain their actual counts without presenting them as native or end-to-end assertions.

summary: Independent full 17-file review is BLOCKED on two reproduced descendant-reparse write-boundary defects. All 41 author Python tests rerun, six author and twelve independent C# checks passed; retained 41+16 and actual 61/30 managed compiler evidence reconciles. No Unity/player/network/Root promotion or authorization was performed.
fixScope: Preexisting descendant reparse write-tree checks before native launch/mutation in Python and staged C# policies
